question: In hospital infection control, Transmission-Based Precautions are considered which level of prevention?
explanation: Transmission-Based Precautions serve as the second level of infection prevention, used alongside standard precautions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: When should a nurse start using Transmission-Based Precautions for a patient?

options.A: At the time of patient discharge from the ward
options.B: When specific routes of pathogen transmission are suspected
options.C: During routine vital sign collection for all admissions
options.D: Only after laboratory confirmation of an infection

explanation: These precautions are applied based on clinical signs before lab results are even ready. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which patients require the use of standard precautions?

options.B: Patients admitted to surgical wards only

explanation: Standard precautions apply universally to every patient care encounter to protect against blood and body fluids. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h2)

question: A nurse touches a patient's intact skin to check pulse. What action is required under standard precautions?
explanation: Touching intact skin does not require gloves, but hand hygiene must be performed before and after contact. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h2)

question: What protective items are needed when entering a room under contact precautions?
explanation: Contact precautions require gloves and a gown to stop germs from spreading from skin or clothing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h3)

question: A patient with a wound infection caused by a resistant bug needs vital signs checked. How should equipment be handled?

options.A: Use bare hands and wash equipment in the utility sink
options.B: Use shared ward equipment after wiping it with water
options.C: Bring all equipment from home for this specific patient
options.D: Keep dedicated equipment inside the patient room

explanation: Leaving dedicated equipment in the room prevents spreading resistant germs to other patients on the ward. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is the maximum distance large respiratory droplets typically travel through the air?
explanation: Large droplets quickly fall to the ground and generally do not travel further than one meter from the source. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which common illness requires the nurse to use droplet precautions?
explanation: Influenza spreads via large respiratory droplets, whereas tuberculosis, chickenpox, and measles require airborne precautions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h4)

question: What type of room airflow is needed for patients on airborne precautions?
explanation: Negative pressure stops infectious air from leaking out into the hallway when the door is opened. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why is a normal surgical mask not enough when caring for a patient with pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: It restricts the nurse's vision during procedures
options.B: It absorbs too much moisture from the breath
options.C: It is too expensive for routine ward use
options.D: It allows microscopic droplet nuclei to pass through

explanation: Surgical masks do not have the tight seal needed to block tiny airborne tuberculosis bacteria. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h5)

question: When putting on personal protective equipment, which item goes on first?
explanation: The isolation gown is put on first to cover your clothing completely before adding other gear. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which of these is an UNSAFE practice when removing personal protective equipment?

options.A: Pulling off the gown from the neck and rolling it away from the body
options.B: Performing hand hygiene between removing different PPE items
options.C: Taking off the respirator mask inside the contaminated patient room
options.D: Removing gloves before taking off the isolation gown

explanation: Respirators for airborne germs should be removed outside the patient room after closing the door to avoid breathing in leftover particles. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: What safety step must a nurse take when cohorting two patients who have the same infection in one room?

options.A: Allow family members to share their bedding
options.B: Keep the ward doors wide open for ventilation
options.C: Ensure adequate spatial separation of at least one meter between beds
options.D: Place beds less than one meter apart without partitions

explanation: Even with cohorted patients, leaving space between beds lowers the chance of cross-infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h7)

question: A patient on droplet precautions needs to be taken to the radiology department for an X-ray. What must be done?

options.A: Ask radiology staff to turn off their ventilation system
options.B: Have the patient wear a surgical mask during transport
options.C: Transport the patient without any face covering
options.D: Transport the patient only during visiting hours

explanation: A surgical mask worn by the patient traps respiratory droplets while moving through public hospital areas. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h7)

question: How can a nurse manage hand hygiene during a water outage in a local Nigerian clinic?

options.A: Use improvised devices like tippy-taps with treated water and soap
options.B: Soak hands in a basin of stagnant water shared by all staff
options.C: Skip hand hygiene until running tap water is restored
options.D: Wipe hands clean with a dry cloth after every procedure

explanation: Improvised running water setups like tippy-taps offer a practical way to wash hands when piped water is unavailable. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h8)

question: What common challenge often affects infection control in primary healthcare settings in Nigeria?

options.B: An overabundance of negative pressure isolation rooms
options.C: Uninterrupted power supply across all wards
options.D: Frequent water shortages and irregular PPE stocks

explanation: Clinics often face challenges with water scarcity and keeping protective gear in stock. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h8)
